paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is an autosomal recessive skeletal disorder resembling osteogenesis imperfecta. Its main features are bone fragility with multiple fractures, which can begin before birth, and severely disturbed ossification of the skull. Patients also have craniofacial malformations such as macrocephaly, frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, and micrognathia (Garbes et al., 2015; Takeyari et al., 2018). In some patients reported with SEC24D mutations, the facial dysmorphism is mild or absent, and these patients have been diagnosed with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (Zhang et al., 2017).

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) reported 3 affected individuals from 2 families with a similar skeletal phenotype. One was a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome. The other 2 were fetuses initially suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta. All 3 had severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures beginning before birth. The 7-year-old boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and downslanting palpebral fissures. Garbes et al. (2015) noted that cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia (CLSD), which is caused by SEC23A mutations, has a largely overlapping craniofacial phenotype. However, CLSD does not feature generalized bone fragility, and the original family with CLSD had cataracts.

paragraphs.text: Zhang et al. (2017) studied 2 Chinese families with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta. The proband in family 1 was a 23-year-old man with recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, an unclosed anterior fontanel, and facial dysmorphism. Three-dimensional CT imaging of his skull showed skull deformities with a broad ossification defect in the frontoapical area, a widened sagittal suture, and wormian bones. The proband in family 2 was a 7-year-old boy who also had recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, and an unclosed anterior fontanel, but no obvious facial dysmorphism.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) carried out whole-exome sequencing in 3 affected individuals from 2 families with a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta. Each was compound heterozygous for 2 of 3 mutant alleles in the SEC24D gene. The alleles were a truncating mutation (Q205X), a missense mutation in a cargo-binding pocket (S1015F), and a missense mutation in the gelsolin-like domain (Q978P). The c.3044C-T (S1015F) mutation lay on a 14-Mb founder haplotype shared by all 3 individuals. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy of skin fibroblasts from the affected boy showed that procollagen was exported inefficiently from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and that the ER tubules were dilated. This closely reproduced the cellular phenotype of individuals with CLSD.
